assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear case of an invention that changed a field: correcting spherical (and later chromatic) aberration made sub-angstrom, atomic-column imaging and spectroscopy routine in materials physics, and the discovery-or-invention criterion is met by an instrument with unmistakable downstream impact on interfaces, defects, 2D materials and catalysts. I weigh this as a specialist in the area, so I note my proximity to the field.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are the multipole corrector theory (Rose), the first working TEM corrector (Haider, with Rose and Urban) and the demonstration on a real instrument and materials problem (Urban). The three credited names map naturally onto theory, realization and application. My recollection is that the STEM-corrector line (Krivanek and colleagues) is a parallel achievement outside the supplied credit, which could complicate a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Corrected instruments have been in broad use for roughly two decades, with wide independent adoption and a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue, relative to the 1998 corrector demonstrations.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM-corrector contribution (not among the credited names) must be recognized alongside the TEM corrector.
Whether the committee regards an instrumentation prize in electron microscopy as sufficiently 'physics' after the 1986 Ruska precedent; this is my recollection and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established strong coherent coupling of a superconducting qubit to a single microwave photon in a resonator, the architecture underlying dispersive readout, gates and most superconducting quantum processors. The idea is original, the experimental demonstration is clean, and the impact on quantum technology and on fundamental tests of light-matter interaction is large.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues supplied the 2004 theoretical proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the 2004 strong-coupling experiment. Three laureates map cleanly onto theory plus experiment. Related contributions on the transmon and on qubit design (Schoelkopf group, Yale) are intertwined but do not require adding names.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation across many laboratories and platforms. The prize in 2025 to macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is adjacent, which is a timing consideration but also shows the committee's openness to the field.
uncertainties: Possible overlap in the committee's eyes with the 2025 circuit prize, leaving a question of sequencing.
Whether the transmon or the circuit-QED architecture is the intended core discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks combine the magic-wavelength trapping idea with narrow optical transitions to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. It is a precise, well-defined invention with a distinct measurable consequence.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group developed the strontium clock to record accuracy and exploited it for many-body and metrological demonstrations. Two names give a compact configuration; Hall already received half of the 2005 prize for frequency-comb related work, which separates the topics.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce the performance, the technology is mature, and a redefinition of the SI second is under discussion. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb prize and from ion-clock work, e.g. by Wineland (2012).
Credit for the lattice idea versus the first operating clocks involves other groups not in the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire materials as a tunable platform for correlated and topological physics. The originality and the pace of subsequent discovery are striking.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation identified the magic angle and the 2018 Jarillo-Herrero experiments showed the insulating and superconducting states. The three names capture theory and experiment, though the experimental cluster (Cao and others) and the Dean, Kim groups' parallel work could raise allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations exist, but interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the full phase diagram is still developing. Recognition is somewhat early, though the core discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Early-career experimental co-authors not among the credited names contributed to the first observations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms gave inertial sensors and measurements of gravity and fundamental constants of exceptional sensitivity. The conceptual step of using light pulses as beam splitters for atoms is original and has produced a durable measurement technology.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard realized early atom interferometers with material gratings, Bordé developed the theory of light-pulse interferometry and Kasevich with Chu demonstrated the light-pulse gravimeter. The credit is spread across several groups and the credited list includes four names, so I pick the three I consider most decisive for the invention; Chu's role is partly covered by his 1997 prize.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and commercial and geophysical applications; maturity is high.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1997 prize for laser cooling and with earlier work on neutron and electron interferometry.
Choice among Bordé, Pritchard, Kasevich and Müller is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and its experimental realization in HgTe wells established a new class of topological electronic states with robust edge and surface conduction. The conceptual influence on condensed matter is large.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed the HgTe route (not credited here) and Molenkamp's group observed the effect; Hasan's ARPES on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 is a separate, also decisive, experimental line. Allocation among theory, two experimental families and an uncredited proposal is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed over almost two decades, with application potential still limited. Timing is reasonable, though credit complexity could delay it.
uncertainties: Absence of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang from the credited names.
Competing experimental claims for the 3D topological insulator discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later giant TMR in MgO-based structures, underlie magnetic random access memory and read heads. It is a materials-and-interface problem in which control of atomic-scale structure was decisive, which I find convincing.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and others achieved giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004, alongside Yuasa and colleagues, who are not credited. The giant spin-valve prize (2007) is a close precedent, which complicates sequencing.
assessment.maturity: Technology is commercial and the physics is well confirmed. Recognition may be considered partly absorbed by the 2007 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize on giant magnetoresistance.
Parallel MgO demonstrations by other groups not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx opened a second family of high-temperature superconductors and a large body of work on pairing, magnetism and nematicity. It is a materials discovery with clear experimental identification.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono's 2008 paper is the origin; the credited pair is natural. Rapid follow-up raised Tc to about 55 K, but those subsequent results come from multiple groups.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and extensively studied, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and the maximum Tc is well below cuprates, which tempers the claim of lasting impact.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would see the discovery as sufficiently transformative compared with the cuprates.
